findings.description: F001's invalid-registry behavior degrades to an empty registry, while F003 treats an empty registry as unbound passthrough. That creates a fail-open path where corrupt worktrees.json disables wrong-worktree protection before plan-mutating commands.
findings.recommendation: Separate valid-empty from invalid-unreadable registry state. Mutating guarded commands should fail closed on invalid worktree registry state, while read-only list/brief/dashboard surfaces can warn and render no rows.

findings.description: F005 only pins dirty, staged, and untracked refusal for remove; it does not explicitly refuse broken bindings, unrelated repositories at the recorded path, non-worktree paths, missing paths, detached HEAD, or branch drift before cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Make remove consume the same worktree-status ownership and drift checks as F004, and require refusal for broken or drifted bindings before any git worktree remove or registry mutation.

findings.description: F004 requires branch drift to be rendered as broken or drifted, but F007's brief, payload, and DOM tests only pin generic clean, dirty, and broken fixtures. Drift visibility could disappear in brief or dashboard while list remains correct.
findings.recommendation: Add a branch-drift fixture to list, operator brief, dashboard payload, and DOM tests, asserting both recorded branch and current branch or an explicit drift marker are visible.

findings.description: F006 says default base is origin's default branch when origin exists, else local main/master, but it does not pin fallback behavior when origin exists without a resolvable origin/HEAD or when both main and master exist locally.
findings.recommendation: Define the exact default-branch resolution order and add tests for origin-without-default-ref, main/master ambiguity, and refusal versus fallback behavior.
